entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (5 subsections) and history note (L. 1961 p. 7 § 14); verified source identity and all five bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked official Smith-Lever Act (7 U.S.C.A. Sec. 341 et seq.) cooperating status (sub 1), prohibited commercial/legislative/unauthorized/preferred-service activities (sub 2), special-service fees, state/national dues ban, and educational-supply exclusion (sub 3), private contributions and equal-opportunity local group cooperation (sub 4), and ban on requiring uniform bylaws or procedures (sub 5). Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: Official county cooperating body under Smith-Lever Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 7 § 14). Recognizes the council as the official county body cooperating with the university under the federal Smith-Lever Act (7 U.S.C.A. Sec. 341 et seq.) and supplementary or related extension acts.

headings.title: Prohibited commercial, legislative, unauthorized, and preferred-service activities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Bars councils from commercial or private enterprises, legislative programs, activities unauthorized by sections 262.550 to 262.620, and giving preferred service to any individual, group, or organization.

headings.title: Service fees, dues ban, and educational-program supplies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits fees for special-equipment or special-personnel services (e.g., soil or seed testing), prohibits collecting or paying dues for state or national organizations, and excludes university-and-council-deemed necessary educational supplies or services from private/commercial activity.

headings.title: Private contributions and equal cooperation with local groups
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits accepting private funds for extension purposes and working through farm, civic, or other groups to reach audiences, provided equal cooperation opportunity is afforded to all county groups and organizations.

headings.title: Prohibition on requiring uniform bylaws or procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Prohibits extension personnel from requiring uniform bylaws, regulations, and methods of procedure.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (11 subsections, including subdivisions, ballot-form paragraphs, and post-ballot continuation paragraphs in subsections 6, 10, and 11), history note (L. 2013 H.B. 542 merged with S.B. 9), and dual effective-date/veto-override notes (Effective 8-28-13 H.B. 542; 10-11-13 S.B. 9 following July 2, 2013 veto and September 11, 2013 override under § 21.250); verified source identity and all 11 bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked charter-county (>950,000) exclusion (sub 2), single-council vs. consolidated governing bodies and powers (subs 3–5), initial tax election with per-county consolidated majority and county-withdrawal option (sub 6), section 262.597 funding exemption/reduction (sub 7), revenue transfer and section 105.688 prudent investor standard (sub 8), untaxed single-council dissolution (sub 9), two-thirds county withdrawal court order with wind-down proviso and Jan 1 effective date (sub 10), and tax-increase election with district-wide consolidated majority and special-fund deposit (sub 11). Revised subsection 10 title to "County withdrawal petition, hearing, ballot, and court order" and subsection 11 title to "Tax increase election, ballot form, approval, and fund"; retained subsections 1–9 titles.

headings.title: Section definitions for extension districts and councils
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(5), history note (L. 2013 H.B. 542 merged with S.B. 9), and Revisor effective-date/veto-override footnote (Effective 8-28-13 H.B. 542; 10-11-13 S.B. 9 after Sept 11, 2013 veto override; see § 21.250). Defines consolidated district, council (under section 262.563), district/extension district, governing body, and single-council district.

headings.title: District formation, charter-county exclusion, and council votes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and effective-date/veto-override notes. Authorizes extension councils (excluding any council in a charter county over 950,000 inhabitants) to form single-council or consolidated extension districts by majority vote of the full council or each participating council.

headings.title: Single-council district governing body and powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and effective-date/veto-override notes. Designates the council as governing body of a single-council district with both sections 262.550 to 262.620 powers and subsection 5 powers; distinguished from consolidated districts in subsection 4.

headings.title: Consolidated district governing body, terms, officers, and meetings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and effective-date/veto-override notes. Sets consolidated-district governing body membership (3–5 representatives per participating council), two-year renewable terms, two-year officers, and at least quarterly regular meetings.

headings.title: Powers and duties of district governing bodies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)–(5) and effective-date/veto-override notes. Covers reviewing council activities/budgets, setting the annual tax rate by September 1, overseeing tax collection and special-fund use, approving payments, and cooperating on programming and equipment.

headings.title: Tax levy election, ballot language, approval, and fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 including ballot-language paragraph and continuation div paragraph, plus effective-date/veto-override notes. Covers permissive submission of a property tax up to 30 cents per $100 assessed valuation at a general municipal election, election costs under section 115.063, statutory ballot form, majority approval rules in single-council vs. consolidated districts (including withdrawal by a rejecting county), and deposit into a dedicated special fund.

headings.title: County exemption or reduction from section 262.597 funding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 including subdivisions (1)–(2) and effective-date/veto-override notes. Applies where the section's tax is levied and collected: exempts the county commission from section 262.597 funding if tax revenue exceeds 200% of the prior three-year average, or permits reducing current section 262.597 funding by 33% of excess tax revenue.

headings.title: Revenue transfer with interest and section 105.688 standard
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and effective-date/veto-override notes. Requires collecting counties to transfer attributable revenue plus monthly interest to the district's special fund, and requires the governing body to comply with the prudent investor standard under section 105.688.

headings.title: Dissolution of untaxed single-council district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and effective-date/veto-override notes. Permits dissolving a single-council district for which no tax has been levied in the same manner as it was formed.

headings.title: County withdrawal petition, hearing, ballot, and court order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 including ballot-language paragraph and post-ballot continuation div paragraph, plus effective-date/veto-override notes. Covers withdrawing a county from a consolidated district via circuit-court petition signed by 10% of recent presidential-election voters, court best-interest hearing, section 115.063 election costs, ballot form, two-thirds voter approval for a withdrawal order with wind-down proviso and January 1 effective date, or petition dismissal. Revised during review from 'Petition, court hearing, and election to withdraw county' to reflect the post-ballot court order and wind-down continuation.

headings.title: Tax increase election, ballot form, approval, and fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 including ballot-language paragraph and post-ballot continuation div paragraph, plus effective-date/veto-override notes. Covers permissive general-municipal-election submission to raise the district tax rate within the 30-cent cap, section 115.063 costs, ballot form, single-council county majority vs. consolidated district-wide majority approval outcomes (distinguished from per-county majority in subsection 6), and deposit into the dedicated special fund. Revised during review from 'Election and ballot form to increase tax rate' to cover the post-ballot approval and fund continuation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and history note (L. 1961 p. 7 § 18); verified source identity and both bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked 10-day pre-office 125% corporate surety bond determined/approved/filed with county clerk and paid by council (sub 1), and mandatory chairman / permissive member suit in own name without joining treasurer upon breach with proceeds applied to council use (sub 2). Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Treasurer surety bond amount, approval, filing, and cost
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 7 § 18). Requires the council treasurer within 10 days of election and before taking office to execute a corporate surety bond of at least 125% of estimated peak funds, subject to county clerk determination, approval, filing, and notice, paid for by the council.

headings.title: Suit for bond breach and application of proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the council chairman (or permits any council member if the chairman does not) to sue in his own name for the council's benefit upon any bond breach without needing to join the treasurer, with collected funds applied to council use.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections) and history note (L. 1961 p. 7 § 19); verified source identity and all four bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked designated public-depository bank deposit (sub 1), exclusive disbursement by secretary warrant or chairman-and-treasurer combination warrant check (sub 2), receipt/disbursement account book (sub 3), and annual written report, term-end settlement, and successor turnover (sub 4). Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Deposit of council funds in designated bank
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 7 § 19). Requires the treasurer to deposit all council moneys in a bank or trust company designated by the council and authorized to receive public deposits.

headings.title: Exclusive warrant or signed check disbursement method
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires disbursement solely by warrant of the council secretary or combination warrant check signed by the council chairman and treasurer, prohibiting payment in any other manner.

headings.title: Treasurer receipt and disbursement account book
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the treasurer to keep an account book recording all moneys received and disbursed, payer/payee, and purpose.

headings.title: Annual financial report, term-end settlement, and record turnover
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires a written annual report at each annual meeting with itemized disbursements and exhibited warrants/checks (recorded by the secretary), term-end settlement with the council, and turnover of books, records, papers, and remaining moneys to the successor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (5 subsections) and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 541); verified source identity and all five bodySha256 fingerprints. headings.title: Appointment, confirmation, and composition of three Missouri delegates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 541). Covers gubernatorial appointment with senate confirmation of three Missouri delegates (dairy producer, consumer representative, and dairy processor) to the southern dairy compact commission under article III of section 262.700.

headings.title: Four-year delegate terms and service duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets four-year delegate terms and states duties to serve diligently and conscientiously toward southern dairy compact purposes.

headings.title: Filling delegate vacancies for unexpired terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires filling vacancies in the same manner as original appointments for the unexpired term.

headings.title: Delegate per diem limit and travel expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes a per diem up to $50 for service and traveling expenses incurred in performing delegate duties.

headings.title: Discretionary appropriation-subject funding by agriculture director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Preserves permissive authority ('may provide') of the agriculture director to fund the delegation as necessary during its term, subject to appropriation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 541); verified source identity and both bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked permissive lawful acquisition and sharing of dairy industry information for the director, delegates, and compact commission (sub 1) and permissive chapter 536 rulemaking for the chapter and compact (sub 2). Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Obtaining and sharing dairy industry information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 541). Authorizes the director of agriculture to obtain dairy industry information by lawful means for use by the director, delegates, and southern dairy compact commission.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking for chapter and compact
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes the director to adopt necessary rules and regulations under chapter 536 to carry out this chapter and the southern dairy compact.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections) and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 541); verified source identity and all four bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked prohibition on violating the southern dairy compact or its rules (sub 1), permissive cumulative $1,000 fine, license revocation/suspension, or fine in lieu thereof (sub 2), daily separate-violation rule (sub 3), and chapter 536 governance of rule fines (sub 4). Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Prohibition on violating compact or compact rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 541). Prohibits any person from violating the southern dairy compact or rules and regulations adopted under it.

headings.title: Fines and license revocation or suspension penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Preserves permissive, cumulative penalties in addition to other legal penalties: a $1,000 fine per violation, license revocation or suspension, or an additional fine in lieu of revocation or suspension.

headings.title: Each day treated as separate violation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Specifies that each day a violation occurs constitutes a separate violation.

headings.title: Application of chapter 536 to rule fines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Subjects fines for violating any rule or regulation to chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (14 subsections, including all subdivisions and verbatim statutory notice text in subsection 8) and history note (L. 2001 S.B. 462); verified source identity and all 14 bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked interest-free assessment abeyance and section 644.027 mandatory-sewer exception (sub 1), 10-acre contiguous farming scope (sub 2), proportionate connection charge and assessment factors retaining archived "connected to such assessments" phrasing (subs 3–4), abeyance end and controlling sections 262.800 to 262.810 (subs 5–6), tolled limitations (sub 7), restricted-delivery notice/180-day/60-day deadlines/preserved dispute right (sub 8), 180-day owner and 30-day political-subdivision circuit-court actions (subs 9–10), local authority preservation (sub 11), public water supply district §§ 247.010–247.227 exemption with crossing-property exception (sub 12), permitted capped initial payment in >=400,000 multicounty cities (sub 13), and AG defense, special assistant AG representation, and political-subdivision fee reimbursement (sub 14). Revised subsection 13 title to "Capped initial assessment payment in qualifying multicounty cities"; retained subsections 1–12 and 14 titles.

headings.title: Abeyance of assessments and section 644.027 sewer exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2001 S.B. 462). Requires the state and political subdivisions to hold water and sewer assessments in abeyance without interest until property improvements connect, except that mandatory sewer connection under section 644.027 does not trigger payment.

headings.title: Applicability to ten-acre contiguous farming tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(2) and history note. Limits section applicability to tracts of ten or more contiguous acres used for farming purposes.

headings.title: Proportionate payment upon connecting property improvements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the owner, upon connecting improvements to the water or sewer system, to pay the proportionate charge for the number of system lines connected.

headings.title: Prohibition on total-cost charging and assessment factors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note. Bars charging based on total cost of running the system to or across the property and bases the assessment on a reasonable hookup charge, proportionate connected-improvement capacity share (retaining archived phrase 'connected to such assessments'), and anticipated proportionate system burden.

headings.title: End of abeyance when farming use ceases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Terminates the abeyance period when the property ceases to be used for farming purposes.

headings.title: Payment terms after abeyance and controlling statutory provisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Makes assessments payable upon end of abeyance under the assessment resolution's terms except where inconsistent with sections 262.800 to 262.810, which control.

headings.title: Suspension of enforcement statutes of limitation during abeyance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Suspends all statutes of limitation for actions to enforce assessment payment while an assessment is held in abeyance without interest.

headings.title: Assessment notice contents, delivery, and preserved dispute right
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 including subdivisions (1)(a)–(f) and (2) and history note. Covers mandatory political-subdivision notice of proposed assessments and Missouri Farmland Protection Act rights, certified restricted-delivery mailing, required verbatim notice text (including 180-day dispute and 60-day protection-claim windows), enclosed act copy, and subdivision (2) preserving the right to contest the assessment amount when claiming protection.

headings.title: Owner circuit-court action disputing assessment amount
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires an owner disputing the assessment amount to file in the county circuit court within 180 days of receiving subsection 8 notice.

headings.title: Political subdivision action disputing act applicability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Requires a political subdivision disputing farmland protection act applicability to file in the county circuit court within 30 days of receiving the owner's protection claim notice.

headings.title: Preservation of local authority to hold assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Clarifies that the section does not diminish county or political-subdivision authority to hold assessments in abeyance.

headings.title: Exemption and crossing-property rule for public water districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Exempts public water supply districts defined in sections 247.010 to 247.227, except that a district may not require payment from landowners whose property is crossed to service another tract until an improvement connects, at which point the farmland protection act applies.

headings.title: Capped initial assessment payment in qualifying multicounty cities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and history note. For a city of at least 400,000 inhabitants located in more than one county, permits an initial payment up to $500 per acre (capped at $10,000) upon final judgment or mutual agreement on the assessment amount as an exception to full abeyance, with all other farmland protection act provisions applying. Revised during review from 'Initial-payment cap in qualifying multicounty large cities' to clarify that this provision permits a capped initial assessment payment.

headings.title: State defense, separate landowner representation, and fee reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history note. Covers joining the state and attorney general defense when a political subdivision challenges sections 262.800 to 262.810, landowner status notice, discretionary appointment of a special assistant attorney general for conflicting arguments (including appeals), and political-subdivision reimbursement of landowner representation costs if it fails to prevail in whole or in part.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (9 subsections, including all subdivisions) and history note (L. 2011 H.B. 458 merged with S.B. 356); verified source identity and all nine bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked Missouri Farmland Trust Act title/purpose (sub 1), trust objectives (sub 2), 5-member advisory board/terms/2-term limit (sub 3), property acquisition (sub 4), Missouri Farmland Trust Fund with post-August 28, 2011 county PILT and optional lessee tax duty (sub 5), property management/20-year beginning-farmer lease guidelines/fees retaining archived "leasing farmland to the trust to beginning farmers" phrasing (sub 6), rulemaking consulting archived "Missouri farmland advisory board" wording (sub 7), broad donor/lessee liability release (sub 8), and chapter 536/§ 536.028/August 28, 2011 nonseverability clause (sub 9). Retained all nine titles as accurate.

headings.title: Short title and farmland preservation and leasing purpose
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2011 H.B. 458 merged with S.B. 356). Titles the section the 'Missouri Farmland Trust Act' and states its purpose of enabling farmland conveyances to the department of agriculture and long-term low- and variable-cost leases to beginning farmers.

headings.title: Creation and objectives of Missouri Farmland Trust
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note. Creates the Missouri Farmland Trust and sets its three objectives: preserving farmland, linking prospective and present farmers, and promoting stewardship best practices.

headings.title: Advisory board creation, recommendations, terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note. Creates the five-member Missouri Farmland Trust Advisory Board (unpaid, appropriation-subject expense reimbursement), specifies its lease/program recommendation duties, and sets five-year terms (July 1–June 30), initial 3/4/5-year staggering, vacancy filling, and a two-consecutive-term limit.

headings.title: Department authority to acquire and hold trust property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes the department of agriculture to accept or acquire agricultural lands, easements, and real or personal property by purchase, lease, donation, or agreement as Missouri farmland trust properties.

headings.title: Missouri Farmland Trust Fund, tax payments, and investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note. Creates the fund in the state treasury with sections 30.170 and 30.180 disbursements, authorizes appropriation-subject administration and county payments in lieu of property taxes for land acquired after August 28, 2011 (at least prior real property tax) plus optional lessee tax payment, bars reversion notwithstanding section 33.080, and provides for state treasurer investment.

headings.title: Contributions, property management, twenty-year lease guidelines, and fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers accepting contributions, improving/operating trust property, mandatory agricultural and stewardship use, rule-based beginning-farmer lease guidelines up to 20 years (retaining archived wording 'leasing farmland to the trust to beginning farmers' without silent edit), and optional lease-application administrative fees.

headings.title: Rulemaking on lessee qualifications, selection, and lease terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Directs department rulemaking in consultation with the 'Missouri farmland advisory board' (archived wording retained) covering lessee requirements, selection, lease terms, renewal, maintenance, and termination.

headings.title: Broad liability release by land donors and lessees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note. Requires any person or entity donating land to or leasing land from the department to forever release the state, department, personnel, and associated persons/entities from injury, death, or property-damage claims relating to participation, negligence/intentional/other acts, and premises conditions.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability condition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Conditions rule effectiveness on chapter 536 and section 536.028 (referencing section 536.010) and declares nonseverability voiding rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2011, if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

Checked 16 definitions retaining archived "United States Office of Budget and Management" phrasing (sub 1), UAZ application, municipal review/modification, 5-/10-year reviews, 25-year mandatory dissolution, and continuation-paragraph permissive noncompliance dissolution (sub 2), 7-member UAZ board governance/hearing/ordinance (subs 3–9), 25-year real property tax abatement cap/reassessment (sub 10), optional grower-UAZ wholesale water/hookup discount (sub 11), sales tax deposits and 50/50 school-district/municipality Urban Agricultural Zone Fund (sub 12), chapter 536/§ 536.028/August 28, 2013 nonseverability clause (sub 13), and 300,000–450,000 charter-county exemption (sub 14). headings.title: Section definitions for urban agricultural zones
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(16) and history note (L. 2013 H.B. 542, A.L. 2015 S.B. 12, A.L. 2018 S.B. 627 & 925, A.L. 2021 S.B. 153 & 97). headings.title: UAZ applications, municipal review, and zone dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and continuation div paragraph, plus history note. Covers applying to an incorporated municipality to develop a UAZ on blighted land, required disclosures (type, jobs, products, SNAP acceptance), municipal review/modification/decision, 5- and 10-year reviews, mandatory dissolution after 25 years, and permissive municipal dissolution during review if requirements are not met.

headings.title: Establishment and seven-member composition of UAZ board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires municipalities planning UAZ designation to establish a seven-member board appointed by school districts (1), other affected taxing districts (2), and the chief elected officer (4 residents, at least one with urban/sustainable agriculture experience).

headings.title: Board member terms, vacancies, and removal for cause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Sets staggered initial terms (5, 4, and 3 years), subsequent five-year terms, holdover service, vacancy filling by original manner, and permissive removal by the appointing authority for inefficiency, neglect of duty, or misconduct.

headings.title: Board quorum and majority voting requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Defines quorum as a majority of board members and authorizes board action by majority vote of members present.

headings.title: Annual election of board chair
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires board members to elect a chair annually from among themselves.

headings.title: Advisory, review, and assessment roles of board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Assigns the board pre-designation advisory duties for the governing body and post-designation review and assessment of zone activities.

headings.title: Public hearing notice, participation, consideration, and continuance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Covers pre-ordinance public hearing scheduling, certified-mail notice to affected taxing districts and political subdivisions, newspaper publication 20–30 days prior, oral and written comment/objection rights, board consideration of evidence, and continuance by motion in the minutes without further notice.

headings.title: Municipal ordinance designating urban agricultural zone
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Authorizes the municipal governing authority to adopt an ordinance designating a UAZ following conclusion of the subsection 8 public hearing.

headings.title: Real property tax abatement cap, duration, and reassessment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Exempts UAZ real property from ad valorem tax increases for up to 25 years as specified by subsection 9 ordinance, capped at prior-calendar-year taxes while used under subsection 1(15), limited to the portion used as a UAZ, with reassessment at abatement's end.

headings.title: Optional wholesale municipal water rates and hookup discount
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Preserves conditional, permissive authority for a municipality providing water services to allow a grower UAZ wholesale water rates and, if available, a 50% standard water-source hookup charge.

headings.title: Sales tax deposits and Urban Agricultural Zone Fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 including subdivisions (1)–(2) and history note. Covers depositing local sales tax revenues from UAZ agricultural product sales and associated vending-UAZ mobile units into the Urban Agricultural Zone Fund (with 1% retained by revenue director for collection costs), fund creation, custody, sections 30.170/30.180 disbursements, section 33.080 nonreversion, investment, and 50/50 allocation between competitive school-district urban-farming grants and participating municipalities.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability condition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and history note. Conditions rule effectiveness on chapter 536 and section 536.028 (referencing section 536.010) and declares nonseverability voiding rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2013, if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Exemption for certain mid-sized charter counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history note. Excludes any charter-form county with more than 300,000 and fewer than 450,000 inhabitants from section 262.900.

headings.title: Hardwood forest product promotion and association contracting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 2023 H.B. 202 merged with S.B. 138), and sunset/termination notes (Sunset date 8-28-29; Termination date 9-01-30). Requires the department of economic development to promote and educate the public on Missouri hardwood forest products and permits contracting with a dedicated statewide association.

headings.title: Hardwood Forest Product Promotion Fund creation and management
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(3), history note, and sunset/termination notes (Sunset date 8-28-29; Termination date 9-01-30). Creates the dedicated fund in the state treasury from grants, gifts, devises, bequests, and appropriations, with sections 30.170 and 30.180 disbursements, biennial nonreversion notwithstanding section 33.080, and state treasurer investment with credited interest.

headings.title: Missouri Sunset Act schedule and section termination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)–(3), history note, and source sunset/termination notes (Sunset date 8-28-29; Termination date 9-01-30). Sets automatic sunset under section 23.253 six years after August 28, 2023 unless reauthorized, 12-year sunset if reauthorized, and section termination on September 1 of the calendar year following sunset.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections, including subdivisions (1)–(4) in subsections 3 and 4) and history note (L. 2014 S.B. 672 merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2016 S.B. 665); verified source identity and all four bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked Farm-to-Table Act title (sub 1), voluntary program creation, archived December 31, 2019 10% local-food goal, coordinator designation, and non-mandatory participation clause (sub 2), four-agency consultation/staff support (sub 3), and coordinator duties (sub 4). Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Short title as Farm-to-Table Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2014 S.B. 672 merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2016 S.B. 665). Names the section the 'Farm-to-Table Act'.

headings.title: Program creation, voluntary participation, goals, and coordinator
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Creates the Farm-to-Table Program in the department of agriculture to connect farmers and institutions, requires voluntary-participation guidelines and goals (including the archived December 31, 2019 target of 10% local food purchases), requires designating an employee coordinator/liaison, and expressly states participation is not required.

headings.title: Interagency consultation and staff support
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)–(4) and history note. Requires the departments of health and senior services, elementary and secondary education, and corrections, and the office of administration to make staff available for consultation and implementation support.

headings.title: Duties of department program coordinator
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)–(4) and history note. Covers coordinator duties including maintaining a farmer-institution website database, state-level leadership, workshops/training/technical assistance, and seeking grants, private donations, or other funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (7 subsections, including subdivisions in subsections 1 and 3) and history note (L. 2014 S.B. 672 merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2016 S.B. 665); verified source identity and all seven bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked definitions scoped to this section, section 262.960, and section 348.407(5) (sub 1), AgriMissouri (§ 261.230) Farm-to-Table Task Force composition including § 324.200 registered dietician (sub 2), local-food procurement mission and contract review (subs 3–4), annual December 31 report (sub 5), permissive public meetings/testimony/information solicitation (sub 6), and voluntary participation/ban on mandatory rules (sub 7). Retained all seven titles as accurate.

headings.title: Definitions for Farm-to-Table provisions and 348.407(5)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(6) and history note (L. 2014 S.B. 672 merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2016 S.B. 665). Defines institutions, locally grown agricultural products, participating institutions, schools, small agribusiness (referencing section 348.400), and small farm (referencing section 350.010) for this section, section 262.960, and section 348.407(5).

headings.title: Task force creation, membership, meetings, and staff support
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Creates the Farm-to-Table Task Force under the AgriMissouri program (section 261.230), specifies agency representatives and appointees (including a section 324.200 registered dietician), designates a department of agriculture chairperson, requires at least two meetings, and authorizes optional department administrative staff assistance.

headings.title: Task force mission for local-food procurement strategies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)–(2) and history note. Defines the task force mission as recommending strategies to incorporate locally grown agricultural products into institutional cafeterias, salad bars, and vending machines and to develop standardized food-service contract language.

headings.title: Review of institutional food service contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the task force to review institutional food service contracts in Missouri to identify standardized language easing local-product procurement and use.

headings.title: Annual findings and recommendations report due December thirty-first
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires preparing and delivering an annual findings and recommendations report to the governor, general assembly, and directors of represented entities by December 31.

headings.title: Permissive public meetings, expert testimony, and information solicitation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Preserves permissive authority ('may hold', 'may invite', 'may solicit') for the task force to hold public meetings, invite expert testimony, and solicit relevant information.

headings.title: Voluntary participation and ban on mandatory rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Clarifies that nothing in the section requires institutional participation and prohibits the department from establishing guidelines or promulgating rules mandating participation.
